new_parts: WOOD TURN (wood_layout.py): 5 nodes, 27 code lines. Hands the bundle on turned a quarter so 'down the piece' means 'along the board' for every shared layer; one setting, Grain Stretch (final 5) makes patches longer along the grain without changing any layer.
CRACKS (cracks.py): 95 nodes, 74 lines. Long thin cracks that start anywhere along a board and taper at both ends, with a pale lip; DAMAGE's cracks only start at a piece edge (the board end).
KNOTS (knots.py): 78 nodes, 64 lines. Core, rings and halo; no shared layer makes rings. Optional.

GRAIN (grain.py): 31 nodes, 59 lines, plus the earlier wood build's 'Wood Grain Gain' box borrowed unchanged (39 nodes, 77 lines). Turns its brightness factor into near-black and pale paint (dark and light streaks, hairlines). Biggest single gain: colour group 0.330 without it, 0.636 with it.
HEIGHT RULE box (height_rule.py): copied from the brick trial, one name changed; tried, scored lower than COMBINE tone blend 0.8, not built in the final recipe.

Soft height bake: a bake option in final_bake.py (Gaussian pixel filter), not a layer; raises height group 0.464 to 0.602 and overall 0.634 to 0.665 on seed set 1 but lowers the normal group 0.569 to 0.498; brick did not use it.

judgement: At a glance it reads as old weathered wooden boards (boards of different heights, dark ragged gaps, long fine grain, cracks with pale lips, knots, rust and grey-blue splatter), and it reads more clearly as planks than the earlier recipe's tile. Next to the reference it is tidy and drawn: straight even boards with a uniform black gap, a butt joint in every board, flat patches instead of big soft dark stains, hatched-looking grain that does not bend round the knots, rings drawn on top of the knots, and no splintered edges. No shared layer needed changing; 86.9 percent of nodes and 84 percent of box code are shared; wood needed one turn, two new layers (CRACKS, KNOTS) and a small GRAIN layer that borrows the earlier wood build's streak box.
failures: First half (stopped helper): Grain Stretch was multiplied instead of divided in round 1 (patterns came out shorter); fixed in round 2.
Round 5 (1254 dots) scored only 0.437, tiling 0.767: a crack core lay on the picture's top edge with its lip across the wrap (my reading by reasoning: chance, not a real seam).
